# lila.debug_draw

Debug drawing in the viewports, after Unreal's DrawDebugHelpers (the Kismet argument order, in snake_case).

```
from lila import debug_draw as dd
from lila.math import LinearColor, Rotator, Vector

dd.draw_debug_line((0, 0, 0), (0, 100, 0), LinearColor.RED, thickness=2)          # gone after 5 s
dd.draw_debug_box(Vector(0, 50, 0), Vector(50, 50, 50), rotation=Rotator(yaw=45))
dd.draw_debug_string((0, 120, 0), "spawn", duration=0)                           # the next redraw only
```

Positions take Vectors or (x, y, z) tuples, colors LinearColors or (r, g, b[, a]) tuples (linear), rotations a Rotator, a Quat or (pitch, yaw, roll). thickness is in pixels.

Every draw has a lifetime: duration seconds, the debugDraw/defaultDuration pref (5 s) when None, the next redraw when 0. A forgotten call clears itself. Draws that stay need persistent=True and a channel, and clearing them is your job:

```
ch = dd.channel("my_tool")
dd.draw_debug_lines(path_points, LinearColor.GREEN, persistent=True, channel=ch)
...
ch.clear()
```

A channel belongs to the extension that makes it and goes when it unloads. Lila clears every channel on File > New and Open, and Show > Clear Debug Drawing (in the hotbox) clears everything.

Calls are safe from any thread. Bad input never draws: NaN, infinite or absurdly far positions are dropped with a warning, segment counts and thickness are clamped. Past the debugDraw/maxPrimitives pref (1M lines and triangles) the oldest draws go first, with one warning. In batch mode draws are kept and expire the same way, with nothing shown.

## Channel

```python
Channel(...)
```

A named group of debug draws with an owner. Draws with persistent=True need one and stay until it is cleared. Lila clears every channel on File > New and Open, and removes an extension's when it unloads.

### Channel.valid

```python
valid: bool
```

Read only.

False once the channel was removed.

### Channel.name

```python
name: str
```

Read only.



### Channel.owner

```python
owner: str
```

Read only.



### Channel.visible

```python
visible: bool
```

Hides its draws without removing them.

### Channel.primitive_count

```python
primitive_count: int
```

Read only.

Lines, triangles, points and texts it holds now.

### Channel.clear

```python
clear() -> None
```

Removes everything drawn into it. The channel stays usable.

### Channel.remove

```python
remove() -> None
```

Clears it for good: later draws into it are dropped.

## channel

```python
channel(name, owner=None)
```

The channel called name, made on first use and owned by the extension calling (or "python" outside one).

Draws with persistent=True need one. Calling again with the same name returns the same channel.

## channels

```python
channels() -> list[lila.debug_draw.Channel]
```

Every channel, Lila's and extensions' included.
